problem: The refile to agsci-3-2 is correct and the labelKey names no plant, but figures.json's alt for the bound crop still reads "several thistle plants with purple-mauve brush-like flowerheads" — and because all three labelKey entries are askedInThisQuestion:true they never render, so that alt is the only figure description a screen-reader user gets and it hands over B's answer on an identification card.

The invented "two human figures" is gone and the ball is now named, but the replacement asserts pose detail the source cannot carry — the embedded sign is 1009x907 px so each pictogram is only ~85x110 px, and isolating the silhouette shows ONE arm raised up-right toward the detached ball with the child mid-stride, not "standing with both arms raised" or a ball "in front of the hands", and the notes restate that pose as verified fact.

The orphan "B:" is properly decoded, but labelKey D still calls the calving jack's lever grip a "T-handle" when the photograph plainly shows a closed D-shaped loop grip — the same detail figures.json's own alt for this very crop records correctly as "a lever with a D-shaped hand grip at its upper end".

Same wrong D description as part (ii) — "a long ratcheted shaft with a T-handle" where the photo shows a closed D-loop grip on the pump lever — and here it matters more, because D is askedInThisQuestion:false so this is one of the two meanings the card actually renders to the student in the "Also on the diagram" panel.

The refile to agsci-3-3-1 is right, but the notes justify it with "machine A is the machine the rest of Q3(b) turns on", which is false against the scheme — part (b)(iv) ("Outline one disadvantage of using B when feeding high producing animals") turns on machine B, the zero grazer this same card also identifies.

The objection was that the bound crop's only visible question — "Suggest one advantage of using a tractor fitted with tracks" — points straight at this card's own credited "improved soil structure or reduces compaction"; the repair changed only the stem's narration, left the crop byte-identical, and the notes then assert "nothing is handed over", so the objection was argued away rather than removed.

The accepts pools and the corrected total of ten options are right, but the recount that was the point of this repair miscounts position: the open "any energy saving measure that a student has not given as an answer to part (a)" clause is the NINTH of the scheme's ten, not "the tenth" (notes) or "the scheme's last clause" (r-1 contextNote) — the tenth and last is "pit silage instead of bales to reduce plastic waste", which the card itself carries in accepts.

The label key still opens "printed twice on this crop" for A and repeats it for B, but the crop prints each of them three times — the banner plus a bracket inside BOTH profiles — which the card's own notes state correctly ("The crop prints A and B three times each"), so the key miscounts the exact letters it was rewritten to decode.

Row r-3 promotes a fifth solidus alternative into a third row of a two-slot "3+1" split and then declares it unclaimable (the sibling q11a-ii models the correct two-row shape), its accepts silently drop two scheme alternatives ("Poor drainage", "poor aeration") that r-1 and r-2 both carry, and the notes' claim that "the stem no longer previews the iron pan, the leached surface or the shallow depth to parent rock" is flatly contradicted by the stem, which quotes "Pale grey, heavily leached", "Darker brown, leached minerals" and the 2 m depth to parent rock.

The old invented clause is genuinely gone, but its replacement rests on something the crop does not show: p13-i0 draws no distinguishable cervix — its only ringed features are two long parallel ridged tubes where the horns meet the tract, and everything from there to the vulva is one smooth undifferentiated tube — so the notes' "including the ringed cervical section the answer depends on" and the contextNote's "the short, thick-walled, ringed section drawn between the vagina and the body of the uterus" send a self-marking student to a landmark that isn't on the drawing (the repo's own figure record for p13-i0 names no cervix, calling that region only "the narrow constricted region where the tubular body of the tract meets the coiled and horned structures").

The replacement label key misdescribes what it claims to have re-rendered: the green route text sits at the lower LEFT (about x=272 on a plan running x≈140–850, only ~70 px right of the red B), not "at the lower right"; it is a single string reading "C Return", not "a small green 'C' and 'C return'"; there is no "third dotted track" beside it (only two beaded routes are drawn, both to its left); and the red B is likewise at the lower left, not "below the middle of the plan" — the repo's own p15-i0 figure record puts all three annotations "at the lower left", and the notes repeat the same wrong description verbatim.

Row r-1's contextNote asserts the trait "has to be a trait you can SEE in one of the two photographs", which contradicts the scheme alternative the same row lists in its own accepts — "AA ‐ smaller calves", a trait no photograph shows (both frames are adult bulls, no calf) — so a student who writes the scheme's third credited trait is told by the card that it does not qualify; the stem also has the page back to front, placing the two photographs "above the line: 'The following are pictures of two beef cattle breeds…'" when that sentence is printed above them on the crop.

labelKey B (and row 2's contextNote, which hangs the 'insect pollination occurs in B' reasoning on it) says 'a bee on one of them', but at native PDF resolution the insect on the chicory petal is a slim black-and-pale-yellow banded hoverfly with a single pair of clear wings, not a bee — and the repo's own verified description of that photograph records no insect at all; labelKey A's 'densely packed' likewise misdescribes a spike whose spikelets are set alternately in two ranks with clear stem visible between them.

The pre-reveal stem still hands the student both marking points: it announces 'a gap between their upper ends' at the ridge and 'a gap between the top of each wall and the eaves above it' at the sides, which are exactly 'going out through roof' and 'arrows coming in at side' — the repo's own figure record calls those two gaps 'the inlet/outlet features the answer depends on' — so swapping the word 'outlet' for the identical geometry reworded the leak instead of removing it.

The rewrite swapped one image-contradicting claim for others: machine A's under-hopper assembly is fully inside the photograph (grass and horizon are visible beneath it, it is merely in deep shadow) so "sits below the bottom edge of the photograph" / "below the frame edge" is false; machine B's applicator hoses are green with black rubber outlet ends, not "black flexible hoses" running to "metal outlets"; and the new stem/notes assertion that the right-hand photograph "has no tractor in it at all" and that the machine "stands alone in a yard" is contradicted by the green John Deere front end and yellow-rimmed wheel occupying its bottom-right corner.

The stem presents "Show your calculation in the box below." as something "the paper adds" to this part, but the paper prints that sentence only under (b)(iii) — (b)(i) carries nothing but an unlabelled "Calculation:" box (confirmed on p33-i0 and p33-i1) — so the card manufactures an on-paper cue that the working itself is demanded, which is precisely the shape of r-1's separate 4 marks for "40 X 57".

The stem hands the student "6448 kg" outright, which is sibling card agsci-2022-ol-q17bii's r-2 marking point verbatim and a number the paper never prints on (b)(iii) — the candidate is supposed to carry their own (b)(ii) answer forward — so the card gives away the sibling's whole answer.

The stem's opening sentence tells the student before reveal that the investigation was to see whether nitrate leached from protected urea 'is less than unprotected urea', which is the substance of the card's single 3-mark point ('farmers should use protected urea as less nitrate is leached when compared to unprotected urea'), so the conclusion can be written without ever reading the bars.

Row r-2's context note calls the closing clause 'not a fourth mark' on a question that has only two awards (the 5 and the 3 the same card correctly describes), so the ordinal is nonsense and implies a third and fourth mark exist.

The notes assert 'the scheme does not say which of the state and the reason takes the 5', but the scheme's own How-to-use page (p.4) states that in a '5+1' tariff the first correct answer encountered takes the 5 and each subsequent one takes 1, and p.24 prints 'Below' above the reason — so the split is determined (State 5, Reason 1), which is exactly what the card's own row notes then assume.

The reveal panel still reconstructs Q1(a): C is decoded as "a low flat white unit ... a lump of soil resting on its top surface and a lit digital display along its front" and r-1's contextNote adds that the drawing's other number is "in grams", which together identify the electronic/mass balance in everything but the word, so the sibling's 3-mark point is paraphrased rather than removed (the display detail is not needed to locate the arrow).

Two stem statements are false against paper p.8: "the paper leaves a single answer line" (part (iii) is given a two-line answer box), and "The captions are what this part is answered from" misstates the credit, which the scheme awards for the DMD figure or the letter ("<67(%) or D"), not for a caption.

The stem's "with the oesophagus entering from the left" is false on the crop — in all three panels the left-hand tube is continuous with the long lower sac the blue A arrow points into, i.e. that chamber's own outlet, while the tube that enters is the one at the top right — and the claim was taken on trust from the figure manifest, whose alt text (rendered as the img alt, pre-reveal) also still states both of Q9(a)(ii)'s marking points ("the rumen enlarges dramatically ... while the chamber marked A becomes proportionally smaller").

Label key A still reads "two or three rounded flowerheads" when photograph A plainly shows four — the count is the figure manifest's wording, not something read off the crop the notes claim was opened and re-opened — and giving both A and C "leaves of three leaflets" puts the trifoliate = clover cue (the very "two of the three are clovers" giveaway stripped from the stem) back into the label key.

r-1's contextNote turns the scheme's bracketed "(using data from graph)" into a requirement — "The last wording is the one that requires the numbers to be quoted — a ranking with no data from the graph behind it is not what the scheme describes" — but the scheme's own front matter (2023-ol.md p.3, lines 74-76) states that a word or term in brackets "is not a requirement of the answer", so the note tells a student to deny themselves a mark the examiner would award.

The notes' claim that "the only stony layer visible is the pale broken rock at the base of the block" is false — the Parent Material band above the rock is drawn with by far the largest dark fragments on the cut face (largest connected dark components ~475/273/259 px versus ~72 px in A's band and ~68 px in B's, and the manifest alt calls them "larger dark stone fragments") — and r-2's contextNote compounds it by seating B's horizon "on the weathering rock at the base of the block", skipping the Parent Material band the diagram draws between them.

The BUILDER note's claim that keeping `notation` on a `fixed` tariff makes the generated module "fail typecheck with TS2353" is false — build-deck.mjs emits the card as an object literal ending `} as SecCard`, and a type assertion suppresses excess-property checking (I compiled this card's exact tariffModel under `tsc --strict`: 0 errors), which is why 397 authored Agricultural Science cards already carry `{kind:'fixed', notation:…}` and 208 of them sit in the shipped higher.ts against a clean typecheck.

Entry B's meaning is a near-verbatim lift of the figures.json alt text — the exact defect the skeptic raised on the sibling card — and it inherits that alt's unverified claim of "several thick pale taproots that run down through the topsoil and the darker band into the tan subsoil", when the crop shows three taproots of which two terminate inside the darker band and the deepest only reaches the top of the tan layer and spreads sideways along the interface, so none actually enters the subsoil and the note's "Figure opened and looked at again during this repair" does not hold.

Row r-4 now presents "belly" to the student as the marking point when the scheme credits "white legs and belly" — a bare belly is not creditable — and the truncation was avoidable, because "white legs" is itself a contiguous run in the extraction and passes the build's own normalise/includes check, so the promoted row misstates the scheme's sixth feature while its contextNote pushes repo paths and build internals into the reveal pane.

The tariff justification misreads the p.4 rule it quotes — p.4 gives the larger mark to the first CORRECT answer encountered, not to the first line of the answer box, so "the paper's answer box fixes that order ... so the split resolves to Picture 3 / Reason 2" does not follow, and the invented fixed split under-pays by a mark the candidate who names the wrong picture but gives a scheme-listed reason (scheme: 3, card: 2).

The sibling leak was relocated rather than removed — on a panel this card itself flags askedInThisQuestion:false, label key B still volunteers "the tallest of the three seedlings", which is verbatim q5a's scheme-accepted reason "seedling is largest in picture B" — and the stem's "the crop is the whole Question 5 block" is false, since p07-i0 stops after part (a)'s answer box and shows neither part (b) (this card's own question) nor part (c), both printed on the same page 7.

The tariff note contradicts itself and the scheme: it says the change makes this card "grade by the same rules and show the same mark values as its sibling agsci-2025-ol-q9aii" and then calls q9aii "the genuinely order-dependent case" (q9aii is modelled fixed 3/2 in the deck, not as an ordered split), and like q5a it converts p.4's "first correct answer encountered" into "first line of the answer box", which p.4 does not say.

The rewritten label key names things that are not on the crop: X is said to be printed "one at each later stage", but the charging-plates stage draws a single cell carrying a blue Y and no X at all, and Y's "inside the heads of the other cells" silently absorbs the two cells whose heads carry a green "?" and are neither X nor Y.

The M/W correction is right on the pixels but it dragged in a new giveaway: label key C's closing clause "not the W the same pattern is usually drawn as" is an editorial aside rather than a description of the crop, and by naming C as the W sampling pattern — the method the syllabus teaches — it hands the student row 1's answer "Method: C" before they answer.
